chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who buys a sacrificial animal (hady) and it had a defect, blindness or something else, he (peace be upon him) said: If he had paid its price in cash, it suffices for him; and if he had not paid its price, he should return it and buy another in its place, a sheep, or a cow.

He (the narrator) said, and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Buy a fat male for the Tamattu' (sacrifice); if you do not find one, then a 'majwūn' (a specific type of young animal); if you do not find one, then from the male goats; if you do not find one, then an ewe; if you do not find one, then whatever is easily available of the sacrificial animals.
He (peace be upon him) said: And for the Tamattu' sacrifice, the jadha' (two-year-old) from the sheep suffices, but the jadha' from the goat does not suffice.

He (the narrator) said, and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said regarding a man who bought a sheep, then intended to buy a fatter one than it: He should buy it, and when he buys it, he should sell the first one. He (the narrator) said, and I do not know (whether he meant selling the sheep or the goat).

key_terms.مَوْجُوءاً: A specific type of young animal

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for buying and sacrificing an animal with a defect in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential nuances of the Hadi (sacrificial animal) for Hajj al-Tamattu', emphasizing that a defective animal is valid if the full price was paid, reflecting the principle of compensation for defects. It establishes a specific hierarchy of preference for the animal's quality and age, distinguishing between sheep and goats, while also providing a practical mechanism for upgrading one's sacrifice. These rulings underscore the Shia emphasis on both the ritual validity and the aesthetic excellence (ihsan) in fulfilling religious obligations.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, regarding a man who buys a sacrificial animal and there was a fault with it, blinded in one eye or something else. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If he has paid cash for it, it would suffice him, and if he did not happen to have paid cash for it, he should return it and buy other than it’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Buy a fat male (animal) for the Tumatto. So if you cannot find, then a cow. So if you cannot find it, then from the virile goats. So if you cannot find, so an ewe. So if you cannot find it, then whatever is easier from the sacrificial animals’.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And it would suffice regarding the Tumatto, the two year old from the sheep, and it would not suffice, the two year old from the goat’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said regarding a man who bought a sheep, then intended that he buys a fat one from it. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So when he buys it, he should sell the first one’. He (the narrator) said, ‘I don’t know (whether he<sup>asws</sup> meant the sheep or the goat)’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“This is about a man who buys an offering which is defective such as blindness, and so on. Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘If he has paid in cash it is sufficient for him. If he has not paid in cash he can return it and buy another.’

Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Buy a fatty male for al-Hajj al-Tamattu‘ (advantageous); if you cannot, then find a mawju’ (cow); if you cannot find it then a male goat, if you do not find, then an ewe, if you cannot find then buy what is available for an offering.’
He (the Imam) said, ‘For al-Hajj al-Tamattu‘ (advantageous) young sheep is sufficient, a young goat is not sufficient.’

About a man who bought a sheep and wanted to buy one more fat, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘He can buy it but he sells the first one.’ I do not know if he (the Imam) spoke of sheep or cow.”
